title: A pesar de que: concession in history

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32: they introduce something that did not stop the main fact. *A pesar de que* is followed by a verb; *a pesar de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive. In history they show resistance against the odds.

items.spanish: A pesar de que eran menos, Hatuey y sus hombres resistieron.
items.english: Although they were fewer, Hatuey and his men resisted.

items.spanish: A pesar de la resistencia, la población taína bajó mucho.
items.english: Despite the resistance, the Taíno population fell sharply.

items.spanish: A pesar de que los españoles enviaron varias expediciones, no pudieron derrotar a Enriquillo.
items.english: Although the Spanish sent several expeditions, they could not defeat Enriquillo.

items.spanish: Pese a las leyes, los abusos continuaron.
items.english: Despite the laws, the abuses went on.

sections.content: After *a pesar de que* use a verb in the indicative for facts that happened (*eran*, *enviaron*). After *a pesar de* use a noun (*la resistencia*) or an infinitive (*a pesar de ser menos*). *Pese a* is a shorter, more formal way to say the same.
